In [[mathematics]], a '''Gregory number''', named after [[James Gregory (astronomer and mathematician)|James Gregory]], is a [[real number]] of the form:<ref>{{cite book|first=John H.|last=Conway|author-link =John H. Conway|author2=R. K. Guy|author2-link=R. K. Guy|title=The Book of Numbers|url=https://archive.org/details/bookofnumbers0000conw|url-access=registration|publisher=Copernicus Press|location=New York|year=1996|pages=[https://archive.org/details/bookofnumbers0000conw/page/241 241–243]}}</ref>

: <math>G_x = \sum_{i = 0}^\infty (-1)^i \frac{1}{(2i + 1)x^{2i + 1}}</math>

where ''x'' is any rational number greater or equal to 1.  Considering the [[power series]] expansion for [[arctangent]], we have

: <math>G_x = \arctan\frac{1}{x}.</math>

Setting ''x'' = 1 gives the well-known [[Leibniz formula for pi]]. Thus, in particular,
:<math>\frac{\pi}{4}=\arctan 1</math>
is a Gregory number.

==Properties==
* <math>G_{-x}=-(G_x)</math>
* <math>\tan(G_x)= \frac{1}{x} </math>

* [[Størmer number]]
